name: Waiter Sweep
description: The Waiter Sweep elevates a controlled leg from deep half guard and manages the opponent's posts so the bottom player can tip the base and come on top.
summary: The Waiter Sweep elevates a controlled leg from deep half guard and manages the opponent's posts so the bottom player can tip the base and come on top.
overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation. Support the lower leg with the arm and shoulder connection while using the legs to help lift.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Lucas Valle — waiter sweep from deep half](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LzphtRQwv6g); [Ryan Hall — the Waiter Sweep](https://ryanhallonline.com/p/waiter-sweep).

attacker.name: Waiter Sweep Attacker
attacker.description: Waiter Sweep (attacker): Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation. Support the lower leg with the arm and shoulder connection while using the legs to help lift.

Use an appropriate sleeve grip in gi or a suitable arm connection without assuming the same grip exists in no-gi. Coordinate leg elevation and post control rather than trying to bench-press the opponent. Follow the hips to a stable top position; pass the remaining leg only if that separate opening exists.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

In Valle's gi demonstration, the collar connection manages the upper body while hip movement brings the lifted leg into the waiting hand; control of the posting sleeve then assists the reversal. Keep the head protected from a crossface as you move underneath. Once on top, establish hip control and balanced chest pressure for the actual landing before beginning a separate pass.

defender.name: Waiter Sweep Defender
defender.description: Waiter Sweep (defender): A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism. Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism. Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction. Avoid leaving the hips directly above an established deep-half shoulder connection.

Return the elevated leg only while the knee can move without twisting. Accept a controlled reversal if balance is lost rather than risking a shoulder or knee. Use inside frames and the remaining leg connection if the opponent comes on top.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

An early escape withdraws the elevated leg or restores a usable post before your weight is carried over the bottom player. If you land underneath, recover frames and knees instead of trying to hold the original standing base through the reversal.
key_principles: Recognize the leg shelf: A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism.
Keep an available post: Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction.
Manage hip position: Avoid leaving the hips directly above an established deep-half shoulder connection.
Recover the leg early: Return the elevated leg only while the knee can move without twisting.
Fall without a locked-arm post: Accept a controlled reversal if balance is lost rather than risking a shoulder or knee.
Retain guard on landing: Use inside frames and the remaining leg connection if the opponent comes on top.
